claims.claim: The Paley graph G_p is d-regular with d=(p−1)/2; adjacent vertices have (p−5)/4 common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have (p−1)/4. Its adjacency spectrum is {d, ((−1+√p)/2)^((p−1)/2), ((−1−√p)/2)^((p−1)/2)}.
claims.evidence: Writing χ for the quadratic character gives degree (p−1)/2 and, from Σ_x χ((x−u)(x−v))=−1 for u≠v with the zero terms handled separately, common-neighbor counts λ=(p−5)/4 and μ=(p−1)/4. Hence A²=dI+λA+μ(J−I−A). On 1⊥ this becomes A²+A−(p−1)I/4=0, yielding the two asserted roots. Neither root equals d; trace A=0 and dimension p−1 give equal multiplicities (p−1)/2. The exact checker confirms the identities on representative admissible primes.
claims.search_method: Quadratic-character proof and strongly regular graph spectral calculation, supplemented by exact enumeration.

claims.claim: Every feasible degree-four moment matrix may be averaged so that its singleton principal block is N=[[1,a1ᵀ],[a1,aI+bA]], where pa is the objective and b is both the moment and diagonal pair-entry of every edge.
claims.evidence: Every map x↦sx+t with nonzero-square s is a graph automorphism. Translations are vertex-transitive, and ratios of two edge differences are squares, so the group is edge-transitive. Averaging simultaneous row/column permutations preserves PSD, moment consistency, clique zeros, normalization, and objective. The invariant vertex moment is a; consistency makes every singleton diagonal a. The invariant edge moment is b, nonedge entries vanish, and M_{e,e}=M_{∅,e}=b because both entries depend on union e. Thus the displayed block and objective pa follow.
claims.search_method: Direct affine-automorphism orbit proof, supplemented by exact orbit and adjacency checks.

claims.claim: SOS_2(G_p)=√p, and hence the elementary hierarchy bound gives SOS_4(G_p)≤√p.
claims.evidence: Let q=(√p+1)/2 be the magnitude of the least adjacency eigenvalue. PSD of the averaged degree-two block gives a−qb≥0 and a+db−pa²≥0. Thus b≤a/q and, for a>0, pa≤1+d/q=√p; a=0 is immediate. Equality is feasible with a=1/√p and b=2/(p+√p): the least-eigenspace and empty/all-ones Schur-complement eigenvalues vanish and all remaining eigenvalues are nonnegative. Every degree-four feasible matrix restricts to a degree-two feasible principal block.
claims.search_method: Exact adjacency-eigenspace decomposition and Schur-complement proof, with quadratic-field certificate checks.

claims.claim: For every finite graph G, SOS_4(G)≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
claims.evidence: For y_v=Ẽ[x_v]>0, L_v(f)=Ẽ[x_vf]/y_v is a normalized degree-two pseudoexpectation: for linear q, moment consistency gives Ẽ[x_vq²]=Ẽ[(x_vq)²]≥0. It fixes x_v=1 and vanishes outside the closed neighborhood, so R_v:=Σ_iẼ[x_vx_i]≤y_v(1+SOS_2(G[N(v)])). If y_v=0, the zero diagonal of the PSD moment matrix forces the entire v row to vanish, hence R_v=0. With t=Σ_vy_v, PSD of the empty/summed-singleton compression gives t²≤Σ_vR_v. Summing the conditional bounds and using t≥0 yields the claim, including the t=0 branch.
claims.search_method: Universal conditioning argument and two PSD Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities; no finite checker is needed.

claims.claim: For nonzero f:F_p→C, |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≥p+1; equivalently, every square minor of the p×p Fourier matrix is nonzero.
claims.evidence: After ordering distinct column exponents y_j, the generalized Vandermonde determinant divided by the ordinary Vandermonde is an integral Schur polynomial. Modulo π=1−ζ, its specialization is ∏_{i<j}(y_j−y_i)/(j−i) in F_p, whose factors are all nonzero. The quotient is therefore nonzero, while the ordinary Vandermonde is nonzero because the ζ^{x_i} are distinct. Hence every square minor is nonsingular. If supports had total size at most p, selecting |supp(f̂)| zeros of f would give an invertible Fourier submatrix annihilating all supported Fourier coefficients, a contradiction; conversely, a singular minor produces such a support violation. Exact cyclotomic enumeration supplements the proof.
claims.search_method: Cyclotomic generalized-Vandermonde proof plus exhaustive exact minor enumeration for p=2,3,5,7.

claims.claim: Let P_- project onto the least-eigenvalue Paley eigenspace and let S_e consist of an edge e and all its common neighbors. With R=|S_e|=(p+3)/4, every real f supported on S_e and equal to 1 at both endpoints satisfies ||P_-f||²≥η₀:=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)).
claims.evidence: The least eigenspace consists of one quadratic class B of (p−1)/2 nonzero Fourier frequencies. If a nonzero vector supported on S_e lay in ker P_-, its Fourier support would have size at most (p+1)/2, whereas R+(p+1)/2=(3p+5)/4<p+1, contradicting claim 4. Thus K=P_-[S_e,S_e] is positive definite. Writing P_-=UU* with normalized Fourier columns, Cauchy–Binet gives det K=p^(−R)Σ_{T⊂B,|T|=R}|D_T|². Each D_T is a nonzero cyclotomic integer. Its nonzero integral field norm and Hadamard's bound R^(R/2) on its other p−2 conjugates imply |D_T|²≥R^(−R(p−2)). Hence det K has the claimed floor. Since K is a compression of a projection, all its eigenvalues are at most one, so λ_min(K)≥det K. Finally ||f||²≥2 from the two fixed endpoints.
claims.search_method: Prime uncertainty, exact Cauchy–Binet expansion, cyclotomic field norm, and projection-compression eigenvalue proof; supplemented by exact Q(√p) checks.

claims.claim: For every prime p≡1 (mod 4), SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, with d=(p−1)/2 and q=(√p+1)/2.
claims.evidence: For an averaged feasible matrix and edge e, let c be the singleton-to-e column and δ=a−qb. The pair diagonal b is nonnegative. PSD after restricting the singleton coordinates to the least eigenspace gives ||P_-c||²≤bδ. If b>0, c/b is supported on S_e and equals one at both endpoints, so claim 5 gives ||P_-c||²≥b²η₀ and therefore b≤a/(q+η₀). The empty/all-ones compression gives pa²≤a+db, hence pa≤1+d/(q+η₀), with a=0 handled directly. If b=0, it gives the stronger pa≤1. Since η₀>0 and 1+d/q=√p, the inequality is strict. The exact checker verifies all algebraic comparisons without floating point on representative primes.
claims.search_method: Projected PSD 2×2 inequality, projection lower bound, and empty/all-ones Schur complement, supplemented by exact quadratic-field checks.

claims.claim: If G is triangle-free and has an edge, then SOS_4(G)=2; in particular SOS_4(G_5)=2.
claims.evidence: Distinct edges have nonclique union, so their moment block is diagonal with nonnegative z_e=M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e}. PSD of the empty/edge block, tested on (−S,1,…,1) with S=Σ_ez_e, gives S−S²≥0 and hence S≤1. If t is the objective, the empty/summed-singleton compression gives t²≤Σ_{i,j}M_{i,j}=t+2S≤t+2, so t≤2. A genuine edge supplies a rank-one feasible clique moment matrix of value two. For p=5, λ=(p−5)/4=0 and d=2, so G_5 is triangle-free and has an edge. The checker verifies the finite graph and its exact feasible matrix.
claims.search_method: Universal moment-block PSD proof plus exact enumeration and rank-one certificate for G_5.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for fixed ε>0, C, and p₀ giving SOS_4(G_p)≤Cp^(1/2−ε) for all sufficiently large admissible primes, or a rigorous proof that this quantified statement is false. The draft proves only SOS_4(G_p)≤√p−dη₀/[q(q+η₀)], where log η₀=−Θ(p² log p). Thus the deficit is exponentially small and the bound is still asymptotic to √p; it cannot yield any fixed-power saving. The draft also supplies no lower bound or other argument negating the quantified statement. Its strict pointwise improvement is correct, nonvacuous partial progress, and its final writeup explicitly states the remaining gap. Therefore target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and the declared PARTIAL resolution is ACCURATE.
